jurisdictions.notes: The list is the Department of Agricultural Resources' Massachusetts Prohibited Plant List as of May 2026, read from the copy Jason saved from mass.gov (www.mass.gov refuses automated readers), with the Department's decisions of December 8, 2025 and May 11, 2026. What the list forbids: the saved pages give no general statement of it; the class sentence is worded from the two decisions, which say of newly added plants that "Agents/Growers will no longer be able to receive new stock, or begin growing new stock, but may sell any existing stock during the phase-out period", so after the phase-out they may not sell it either. The list page's own statement of scope was not among the saved pages. Legal basis: neither the list nor the decisions names the law it is made under. Each decision follows a public hearing and written comments, and finds that the plants "pose a threat to land in Massachusetts". M.G.L. c. 128, §27 lets the director, after a public hearing, prohibit the delivery into the Commonwealth of plants likely to carry pests or disease, and make rules to carry out §§16 to 31; §29 fines violations of §§16 to 27, and of orders and regulations made under them, $10 to $100. The University of Massachusetts Extension's manual (not official) says the Department cites c. 128, §2 and §§16 to 31A. Phase-outs (the list's asterisk): Chinese silver grass, Miscanthus sinensis, December 8, 2025 through December 31, 2026; jetbead, Rhodotypos scandens, December 8, 2025 through December 31, 2027; black alder, Alnus glutinosa, December 8, 2025 through December 31, 2028; sapphire berry, Symplocos paniculata, May 11, 2026 through May 11, 2028; Japanese angelica tree, Aralia elata, May 11, 2026 through May 11, 2029. Until each date the plant is listed (nurseries may sell existing stock); after it, it should move to the class prohibited (ban). The phase-out classes say "after" the last day of sale; the decisions don't restate the ban itself. Callery pear, Pyrus calleryana, is also asterisked, but its phase-out dates are in the Department's November 2022 update, which was not saved; plants whose phase-outs ended years ago (Japanese barberry, burning bush) carry no asterisk, so its phase-out was presumably still running in May 2026: listed until its dates are read. Permits and exceptions, each said in its own line (classes prohibitedPermit and prohibitedBonsai): water spinach, Ipomoea aquatica, is printed "[PERMIT REQUIRED – contact MDAR]"; Japanese black pine, Pinus thunbergii, "[Limited exceptions for bonsai growers, contact MDAR for details]". Water chestnut, Trapa natans, is on the list and also banned by statute (M.G.L. c. 128, §20A: "No person shall knowingly plant, transport, transplant or traffic in plants of water chestnut (Trapa natans) or in seeds or nuts thereof nor in any manner cause the spread or growth of such plants"; fine $10 to $100, §29): shown by the statute's class. Genus entries ("spp."): Aeginetia, Alectra and Striga. Cape tulip, printed "Homeria spp.; Moraea spp.", is not entered: Homeria is now part of Moraea, and Moraea read whole would take in every Moraea, garden species included; the federal list names the Cape tulips (Moraea collina, M. flaccida, M. miniata, M. ochroleuca, M. pallida). Left out: "Non-native Orobanche spp." and "Non-native Cuscuta spp.", since the list names neither the natives it spares nor the others (the federal list's genus entries, which except the natives by name, already cover the non-native broomrapes and dodders); Caulerpa taxifolia, an alga. Synonyms printed after a semicolon are recorded as other names ("also"), "ssp." written "subsp.": Egeria densa (Elodea densa, Anacharis densa); Digitaria abyssinica (D. scalarum); Frangula alnus (Rhamnus frangula); Mimosa diplotricha (M. invisa); Fallopia japonica (Polygonum cuspidatum, Reynoutria japonica); Salix atrocinerea (Salix cinerea ssp. oleifolia); Ficaria verna (Ranunculus ficaria); Monochoria vaginalis (Pontederia vaginalis); Centaurea biebersteinii (C. stoebe ssp. micranthos); Carthamus oxyacanthus (C. oxycantha). Misspellings: "Lycium ferrocissimum" (L. ferocissimum); "Setaria pallidifusca; S. pallidefusca; S. pumila" entered as the first, with the second as its spelling; S. pumila, yellow foxtail as a whole, is not added as another name (the common names printed are "cattail grass, yellow foxtail"; the federal list names the plant Setaria pumila subsp. pallidefusca); "Pennisetum polystachyon; P. polystachion" entered as the first, with the second as its spelling. Hybrids: Bell's honeysuckle is printed "Lonicera x bella [L. morrowii x L. tatarica]", entered as Lonicera × bella. Plume grass is printed "Miscanthus sacchariflorus (also covers Miscanthus x giganteus, a hybrid of M. sacchariflorus and M. sinensis)": the species is entered, and Miscanthus × giganteus too, since the list names it. Kudzu is printed Pueraria montana (check it matches the catalog's kudzu, Kew's Pueraria montana var. lobata). The list excepts no native forms: Phragmites australis includes the native subspecies americanus, and Phalaris arundinacea its native populations; black locust, Robinia pseudoacacia, variable water-milfoil, Myriophyllum heterophyllum, velvet mesquite, Prosopis velutina, and tornillo, Prosopis reptans, are native elsewhere in North America. Not read: 330 CMR 9.03, the currant and gooseberry (Ribes) quarantine (mass.gov). Left out: §24 (abatement of land overgrown with noxious weeds; it names no plants), the seed law (c. 128, §§84 to 101), and advisory lists, among them the Massachusetts Invasive Plant Advisory Group's. Reviewer (2026-10-31): the class sentences for phase-outs name the date after which the plant is prohibited; still to read, from mass.gov by hand: the list page's own statement of what the list forbids, and the November 2022 update with Callery pear's phase-out dates. Kew's accepted names (2026-10-31), by which these are also matched: Pennisetum macrourum as Cenchrus caudatus; Egeria densa as Elodea densa; Eichhornia azurea as Pontederia azurea; Prosopis strombulifera as Strombocarpa strombulifera; Leptochloa chinensis as Dinebra chinensis; Cynanchum louiseae as Vincetoxicum nigrum; Emex spinosa as Rumex spinosus; Salvinia herzogii as Salvinia biloba; Humulus japonicus as Humulus scandens; Fallopia japonica as Reynoutria japonica; Prosopis pallida as Neltuma pallida; Pennisetum clandestinum as Cenchrus clandestinus; Pennisetum pedicellatum as Cenchrus pedicellatus; Ficaria verna as Ranunculus ficaria; Polygonum perfoliatum as Persicaria perfoliata; Monochoria hastata as Pontederia hastata; Cynanchum rossicum as Vincetoxicum rossicum; Monochoria vaginalis as Pontederia vaginalis; Senecio jacobaea as Jacobaea vulgaris; Emex australis as Rumex hypogaeus; Prosopis reptans as Strombocarpa reptans; Prosopis velutina as Neltuma velutina; Mycelis muralis as Lactuca muralis; Salsola vermiculata as Caroxylon vermiculatum. Matched only as printed (Kew gives no one accepted species for them, or a broader one): Setaria pallidifusca, Pennisetum polystachyon, Ampelopsis brevipedunculata, Centaurea biebersteinii.
